name: appstorepack
description: Create App Store screenshots, app icons and App Store copy for iOS apps from chat, then export the bundle or push it to App Store Connect.

interface.longDescription:
AppStorePack makes the App Store listing for your iOS app from the chat: screenshots, app icon and App Store copy, ready to export or push to App Store Connect.

What you can do:
- Start a project for your app and choose from 48 App Store screenshot templates, previewed with sample screens.
- Add your app screenshots and logo through an upload panel in the chat. Files go straight to AppStorePack, not through the conversation.
- Write short captions for each screenshot panel and preview the whole set for iPhone, plus iPad and iPhone Duo if your app supports them.
- Turn your logo into the 1024x1024 App Store icon, then adjust its background and size.
- Write the name, subtitle, keywords, promotional text and description, checked against Apple's character limits and rules before they're saved.
- Make the optional App Store creative assets: the product page header and search results images.
- Export a bundle with full-resolution screenshots, the icon and the copy, or push the text and screenshots to your app in App Store Connect.

Who it's for: developers and small teams shipping iOS apps who want a finished App Store listing without a design tool.

Limitations:
- You sign in to an AppStorePack account when you connect.
- Whether you can export the bundle or push to App Store Connect depends on your AppStorePack plan. AppStorePack tells you early if your account doesn't include them.
- Pushing needs an App Store Connect API key, added on your AppStorePack Account page. You see exactly what will change and confirm before anything is pushed. A push replaces the screenshots on the app's editable version and never submits the app for review.
- AppStorePack makes App Store listings only, not Google Play listings. It lays out the screenshots you provide; it doesn't capture screenshots of your app.
capabilities: Design App Store screenshots from templates
Upload screenshots and a logo in the chat
Make the App Store icon from a logo
Write App Store copy within Apple's limits
Push the listing to App Store Connect
defaultPrompt: Make App Store screenshots for my iOS app.
Write my app's App Store subtitle and keywords.
Turn my logo into an App Store icon.

positive.description: Show a project's screenshot design. The test account has a sample project, Basil, a meal planner.
positive.prompt: Show me the screenshot design for my Basil project.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the Basil project and shows one image with its five iPhone screenshot panels side by side, each with an app screenshot and a caption.

positive.description: Start a new project and pick a screenshot template.
positive.prompt: Start an AppStorePack project for my habit tracker app Streakly and suggest a screenshot template.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates a project named Streakly, shows the image of all screenshot templates, and recommends templates that suit a habit tracker, saying why each fits.

positive.description: Open the in-chat upload panel for screenshots and the logo.
positive.prompt: I want to add new screenshots to my Basil project.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the AppStorePack upload panel for Basil in the chat, with a tile for each of its five iPhone panels (each marked as added) and one for the app icon. Dropping a PNG or JPEG on a tile uploads it and marks the tile with the file name.

positive.description: Rewrite App Store copy within Apple's limits.
positive.prompt: Rewrite Basil's App Store subtitle to focus on saving time.
positive.expected_behavior: Saves a new subtitle of at most 30 characters about saving time and shows the saved text. The other App Store copy fields don't change.

positive.description: Export the App Store bundle. The test account's plan includes export.
positive.prompt: Export the App Store bundle for Basil.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a download link, valid for one hour, to a zip with Basil's five full-resolution iPhone screenshots, the 1024px app icon and the App Store copy.

negative.description: Submitting an app for App Review is out of scope: AppStorePack never submits apps for review. Expected: Doesn't call any tool that changes data. Explains that AppStorePack can't submit apps for review and that submission happens in App Store Connect.
negative.prompt: Submit Basil to Apple for App Review.

negative.description: Projects can't be deleted from the chat; there is no tool for it. Expected: Doesn't delete or change anything. Explains that projects can't be deleted from the chat and that each one can be deleted on the Projects page at appstorepack.com.
Google Play publishing is outside the supported iOS App Store workflows. Explain this limit without invoking AppStorePack tools or claiming a listing was created or published.
negative.prompt: Create and publish a Google Play listing for my Android app.

review.commerce_description: Users purchase a subscription on the AppStorePack website. The subscription enables downloading exported assets and the App Store Connect package bundle, and pushing the listing to App Store Connect. No purchases take place in ChatGPT.
prompts: Make App Store screenshots for my iOS app.
Write my app's App Store subtitle and keywords.
Turn my logo into an App Store icon.

publication.release_notes: First release. Design App Store screenshots from 48 templates, add screenshots and a logo through an upload panel in the chat, write captions and App Store copy checked against Apple's rules, make the app icon, then export the bundle or push the listing to App Store Connect.
